video.description:
Learn to explain how an app notices when the connection changes: Reachability, NWPathMonitor & Network Path, with real code, a quiz at the end and each example read twice (normal, then slow).

Today's terms
Reachability - Whether the device can reach the network right now.
NWPathMonitor - An Apple class that watches the network and tells your app when the connection changes.
Network Path - A snapshot of the current network connection, such as its status and whether it is expensive.

Quiz at the end - write your answers in the comments, then watch again to check.

landscape.hook: Can you explain Reachability, NWPathMonitor and Network Path in English?

dialogue.title: Am I online?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Jake, the upload fails with no message when the phone is offline.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Check reachability first. It tells you if the device can reach the network.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Should I test it once before each request?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: That is not enough, because the connection can change at any time.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: So how do I watch it?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Use an NWPathMonitor, like `monitor` in our code.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: What does the NWPathMonitor give me?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: A network path, in `pathUpdateHandler`. It is a snapshot of the connection.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Yes. If the network path is satisfied, we are online.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Then I can show a banner when it changes.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Right. Call `start` on the NWPathMonitor, and update the banner from the network path.
Check reachability before you upload the photo.
